name: Brand expressive
summary: Big display type, vivid color and springy motion, for launches that must be remembered.
description: Brand expressive is an Open DS scheme: a full set of answers to the Open DS grammar, with the reasons behind each, usage rules, voice and tone, and the tokens that follow. Big display type, vivid color and springy motion, for launches that must be remembered.

ai.use_when: Launch sites, campaigns, marketing pages and consumer brands that lead with personality.
ai.avoid_when: Tools people use for hours, or forms where calm matters more than character.

scenarios.text: A visitor lands on a launch page from a social post and joins the waiting list.
An agency swaps the campaign colors for the next drop without changing the components.

summary.text: Playful and short. Big words, few of them.

principles.text: Headlines are short and bold. Three to six words.
Verbs that move: Join, Try, Go.
Playful in headlines, plain in errors.
A button label stays on one line: it never breaks onto two.

out.why: Brand expressive keeps only the parts in use for one action and a story, not a part for one campaign. Sharing files in a conversation is neither.
Brand expressive keeps only the parts in use for one action and a story, not a part for one campaign. A back-and-forth chat is neither.
Command serves expert users who type to jump anywhere. Brand expressive serves new customers deciding if they care, who come from social posts on their phones.
Context menu is for power users, and people who don't know to right-click never find it. Brand expressive serves new customers deciding if they care.
Brand expressive avoids tools people use for hours. Data table is for acting on many records in bulk; here people browse and explore the story.
Touch screens have no hover, and visitors come from social posts on their phones. Popover already opens a product preview on tap.
Visitors come from social posts on their phones, and they are new customers deciding if they care. A keyboard shortcut serves neither.
Brand expressive keeps only the parts in use for one action and a story, and a visit lasts a few minutes. A long conversation split into days is neither.
Menubar is for dense desktop tools and not phones. Visitors come from social posts on their phones, and the site sections use navigation menu.
Brand expressive keeps only the parts in use for one action and a story, not a part for one campaign. A live conversation is neither.

Phones first: drawer is the bottom panel for phones and already holds the menu, and dialog holds the waitlist form.
Sidebar is for apps people move around all session. Brand expressive avoids tools people use for hours, and a visit lasts a few minutes at most.

answers.question: brand.q3
answers.why: Bricolage Grotesque for display and headings, DM Sans for text: loud where the brand speaks, easy where people read.

considers.readability: Body text sits in DM Sans, a low-contrast sans that reads easily in short copy.
considers.legibility: DM Sans keeps simple, open shapes at small sizes; the display face never sets small text.
considers.scalability: Both are variable: Bricolage Grotesque has optical size, width and weight axes, and DM Sans optical size and weight.
considers.numerals: Numbers are few and set in DM Sans, in short copy rather than tables.
considers.scripts: Latin, with accents; other scripts need faces chosen for the same voice.
considers.recognition: Bricolage Grotesque's character is the brand's: people know it by its headlines.
considers.familiarity: DM Sans for text keeps reading familiar while the display face takes the risks.
considers.personality: Bold and confident, as the brand answer asks.
considers.performance: Two variable families, one file each.
considers.licensing: SIL Open Font License, both: free to embed in apps and on the web.
considers.fallback: Falls back to system-ui, as its tokens say; DM Sans is the display face's text pair.

color.$description: Color options: raw hue ramps. Each hue has a light ramp and a dark ramp (the same steps tuned for dark backgrounds). Steps only: each theme decides its own base (@). Themes pick from these; components never read them.

taupe.$description: The taupe hue: a light ramp, a dark ramp and its base value.

150.$description: Derived: the step between 100 and 200 on the scheme's step curve (even-ease), even in contrast. Added so a floating layer sits one step above raised in dark.

400.$description: Derived: the OKLab midpoint of 300 and 500. Added so muted text can pass 4.5:1 and stay quieter than secondary.

600.$description: Derived: the OKLab midpoint of 500 and 700. Added so muted text can pass 4.5:1 and stay quieter than secondary.

100.why: This step is the soft background of status messages in light mode and the status text in dark mode. As generated, the text looked white on dark backgrounds, so the step got a little more color, and blue and red a touch darker, until the color showed.

space.$description: Space options. Names give the size in pixels at the default text size; values are rem.

size.$description: Size options for controls, rows and icons.

round.$description: A circle of a square: avatars, radio dots, thumbs and round buttons.

pill.$description: A capsule of any box: tracks, progress, the scroll thumb and pill controls.

size.$description: Type size options. Names are pixels at the default text size; values are rem, so text grows with the user's setting.

line-height.$description: Line height options: ratios of the text size. The type scale generates them.

family.$description: Font family options. Each brand's theme picks its display, body, interface and data fonts from these.

fast.$description: Fast: about 120ms, the convention for feedback.

moderate.$description: Moderate: a calm, easy-to-follow speed, about 200ms.

relaxed.$description: Relaxed: a slower speed for larger moves, about 320ms.

spring.$description: A spring that overshoots and settles back. Only for the emphasize move.

standard.$description: A standard ease-out: fast at the start, settling slowly, with no overshoot.

strong-out.$description: A strong ease-out: most of the way in the first third of the time, then a soft stop. For exits.

accelerate.$description: An accelerate curve: slow at the start, fastest at the end. Only for a layer that leaves the screen.

shadow.$description: Raw shadows. Elevation semantics point at these.

card.$description: Raw shadow for card in light mode.

overlay.$description: Raw shadow for overlay in light mode.

overlay-dark.$description: Raw shadow for overlay in dark mode.

1_75.$description: An icon stroke width option, on Lucide's 24px grid.

open-ds.why: A touch target sets the 52px default. Compact is one 8px step below it; large is one step above it, for the one loud sign-up action. The scheme has no row role, so a row takes the default.
Spacious: big space makes big moments, so panels double their room; rows stay tight.

shorthand.description: What each semantic token does for people in this scheme, in a headline and one line. The token map card shows it.
